what: What to prompt for in each scene, and what class the result carries. SAM is class-agnostic -- it returns a mask and never a name -- so every `label` below comes from the scene FOLDER NAME plus the object that was prompted, and never from a model. A wrong class here is a wrong line in this file, which is why it is committed beside the labels.
why_text_prompts: The folder name names the SUBJECT, not the only object. Timo is in the *-box-* scenes (which is why the shipped detector emitted 421 and 490 `person` boxes there) and may be in the *-lite3-* ones. Prompting each object separately is what keeps a person out of the `lite3` class and a robot out of `person`.

dim-lite3-in-difference-distance-and-ang.expect: one Lite3 quadruped walking. No person was visible in 10 frames sampled across the clip.

light-lite3-in-difference-distance-and-a.expect: one Lite3 quadruped walking. No person was visible in 10 frames sampled across the clip.

dim-box-in-different-distance-and-angle.expect: a person carrying and positioning a cardboard box. Both are present; only the person is labelled, because there is no box class in a 22-class net whose one new class is `lite3`.

light-box-in-different-distance-and-angl.expect: a person carrying and positioning a cardboard box.

dim-people-walk-around.expect: people walking, often truncated by the frame edge at close range.

light-people-walkaround.expect: people walking, often truncated by the frame edge at close range.

phrase_sweep.what: OWLv2 is extremely sensitive to wording, and the natural phrase is the worst one. Twelve phrases were scored on 5 keyframes of each quadruped scene at threshold 0.02; `probe_queries.py` is the sweep and `phrase_sweep.json` is its output.

measured.a robot dog: 0.000 on all 10 frames — the phrase anyone would try first
measured.a robot: 0.068-0.169, and the box is on a ceiling fitting
measured.a small white four-legged machine: 0.305-0.629 light, 0.376-0.574 dim — the one that works

phrase_sweep.lesson: A phrase that reads like the object's NAME loses to a phrase that reads like its DESCRIPTION. This was measured, not guessed, and it is the difference between 0 and 60 labelled frames in the light quadruped scene.

thresholds.what: Per-query OWLv2 score floor. Both are 0.22, set from a 28-frame hand-check and NOT from the score distribution.
thresholds.why: At the first pass's global 0.12 the hand-check scored lite3 23/24 but person only 9/16, and every person failure sat at 0.12-0.20 while every success sat at 0.21+. The floor is where the hand-check turned, which is why the sheets are committed.
thresholds.cost: 0.22 keeps 95% of lite3 (131/138) and 51% of person (259/505). Half the person boxes are discarded to buy precision, because a wrong box poisons a training set and a missing one only makes it smaller.
